best_field_traits: REVERCHON'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): the existing real photo shows a skinny, often interrupted upright flowering head, with widely separated spikelet groupings. Its bristles are sparse—some spikelets appear almost unbristled—but FNA gives bristles about 2–8 mm where present; do NOT teach a hard ≤2 mm cutoff. Seek short knotty rhizomes, the stiff hair ligule (1–2 mm), and mature 2.1–4.5 mm spikelets. No bristle measurement is visible in the original picture.
Texas perennial often forming a small to moderate upright tuft from shallow, hard, branched rhizomatous bases.
Fine basal blades; narrower stem blades often only a few mm wide.
Loose/slender, often broken or interrupted spike-like panicle, in local treatment about 5–15 cm long.
Spotted purplish 3–3.6 mm spikelets in local flora treatment; observe mature structures before claiming exact ID.
True ligule can form a hair curtain around 1–2 mm; hairs in the leaf collar can be longer and must not be mistaken for the ligule.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole flowering head next to centimeter ruler, showing interrupted spacing
Several intact mature spikelet bases viewed 10–20×: bristles absent on some branches or 2–8 mm when present
Short knotty rhizome and attached culm on legal collection
Actual 1–2 mm stiff-hair ligule distinct from longer nearby collar hairs
Spikelet/glume macro with mm scale; native county audit remains unchanged
crew_field_check: First find the WHOLE panicle and compare crowded/loose head arrangement without forcing species from silhouette.
Inspect an intact attached SPIKELET at 10–20×. Count the SUBTENDING PERSISTENT BRISTLES (sterile branches), not grass awns or protruding flower parts.
Record bristle count/length and spikelet length using a 1-mm scale, and compare the same-plant collar ligule.
Check a rooted base only where collecting is legal: annual fibrous millet vs knotty rhizomatous perennial parviflora/reverchonii, and perennial scheelei.
Existing archival images do not prove every underlying bristle count or rhizome; if unresolved identify Setaria sp.
next_photo_sequence_20261023: Verify existing three JPEGs display on the ordinary public species gallery; inspect actual image pixels before assigning anatomy markers.
Get rooted whole plant with head and foliage visible, not only one detached head.
Show entire attached inflorescence and several spikelet base close-ups.
Photograph attached collar true hair-fringe ligule with 1 mm ruler.
Photograph attached mature spikelet plus persistent sterile-branchlet bristles and 1 mm scale; record species-appropriate numbers and measurements.
Finish with matched Setaria reverchonii, scheelei and parviflora comparative head/base photo, arrows only on clearly resolved structures.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with S. parviflora, Reverchon's bristlegrass has a more interrupted narrow head and much fewer attached bristles (parviflora typically 4–12 per spikelet). S. scheelei has conspicuously long spreading bristles commonly 10–35 mm and a longer tapering head, often broad hairy leaves. Millet S. italica is an annual crop/escape with heavy dense terminal heads. Panicle texture varies with maturity, so verify bristles at the spikelet base.
not_reliable_alone: Color or texture of seedhead without bristle group macro
Bristles mistaken for true floret awns or flower stigmas
Mature spikelet counts read from a photo too small to show attachment
Cultivated or habitat context presented as confirmed local nativity

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: On a perennial with short sometimes knotty rhizomes, trace the narrow, often INTERRUPTED erect panicle and inspect several spikelet bases: sparse bristles can be absent on some portions; when present generally 2–8 mm, not a hard ≤2-mm cutoff.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_growth_and_collar: Perennial with short sometimes knotty rhizomes; culms ~30–90 cm. Narrow blades ~1–7 mm; ligule a 1–2-mm fringe of stiff hairs at actual blade/sheath junction. Sheaths can carry papillose-based hairs; distinguish longer collar hairs from the true ligule fringe.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_inflorescence_and_bristles: Erect slender interrupted panicle ~5–20 cm; scabrous rachis; sparse persistent sterile branchlet bristles, ~2–8 mm where present. Mature spikelets elliptic to obovate ~2.1–4.5 mm. Measure several attachments on a single confirmed plant.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_spikelet_glumes_lemmas_awns: Lower glume approximately 1/2 spikelet length, 5–7-veined; upper glume about as long as upper fertile lemma, 7–9-veined. Lower sterile lemma near fertile lemma length, lower palea absent. Upper fertile lemma firm, finely cross-wrinkled; upper palea similarly firm. Spikelets lack true long glume/lemma awns: do not mistake subtending bristles for awns.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: S. parviflora has short dense even-width heads, 4–12 bristles per spikelet and knotty rhizomes; S. scheelei has a long tapering head and usually single 10–35-mm bristles; introduced S. italica has a heavy dense head and annual fibrous roots. Never identify from interrupted head silhouette alone.

Several 10–20× mature spikelet attachments, including truly absent versus present 2–8-mm bristles, with mm scale; no invented arrow on invisible bristle.
Exposed 1–2-mm stiff hair ligule separate from sheath-mouth hairs with mm ruler.
Dissected mature spikelet showing both glumes, sterile lemma and transversely rugose fertile lemma; paired scale-matched S. parviflora and S. scheelei.

items.why_it_matters: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.

rights_held_comparison_items.why_it_matters: SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Setaria — the bristle count is on a real spikelet
steps: START with the local Eric Knight interrupted-head overview (panel 1). Two Patrick Alexander CC0 photographs have now been JPEG/pixel inspected: panel 2 shows distinctly spaced real spikelets along the axis; panel 3 shows narrow leaf and hairs at its junction. Four new arrows point only to those gross photographed structures.

FIND THE BRISTLE ON THE BRANCHLET, NOT ON THE SPIKELET: in the narrow Austin/UT treatment a bristle is borne by a ringlike thickening near the base of a branchlet spikelet, with some upper solitary spikelets lacking one. Photograph insertion under 10–20× before drawing arrows.

RECONCILE BRISTLE SIZE: local UT specimens describe curved bristles to about 2 mm; Flora of North America reports a broader 2–8 mm range. Neither is a measurement taken from the existing photos. Record specimen and maturity, not a universal ≤2 mm cutoff.

MEASURE an attached mature spikelet beside a millimeter ruler. FNA gives 2.1–4.5 mm, while the UT local treatment gives approximately 3–3.6 × 1.7–1.8 mm. Distinguish the short lower glume (usually 5–7 veined) from the longer upper glume (7–9 veined), and the hard wrinkled fertile lemma.
AT THE TRUE COLLAR, photograph the 1–2 mm stiff-hair ligule separately from long sheath pubescence. Both are unproven by the existing three photographs.

ROOTED BASE: look for short hard/knotty rhizomes of a perennial plant. Compare knotroot S. parviflora with numerous bristles versus S. scheelei with longer obvious bristles. Do not mistake terminal solitary unbristled spikelets for another species.
Keep the card FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until actual 10–20× scale views show the bristle insertion, counted structures, true ligule and rhizomatous base on an authenticated individual.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Sparse interrupted flowering axis + fewer bristles, sometimes absent at terminal upper spikelets; verify BRISTLE INSERTION on branchlet and perennial knotty base, not a guessed hair arrow.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Three exact-species JPEGs already physically archived, all three featured; existing first-panel gross arrows preserved. UT local bristle description (to ~2 mm) and FNA broader range (2–8 mm) differ by source/scope. No photo in this gallery resolves the bristle base, ligule or glume nerves with a calibrated scale. No new JPEG or fine arrow asserted. 2026-10-26: CC BY-NC S. scheelei comparative panel swapped for verified-in-repository CC0 S. scheelei whole-plant comparison; three inherited original-pixel gross arrows, not new bristle-level evidence. Two Patrick Alexander archived JPEGs were independently pixel-inspected at source 3600×2400 October 26, and found clean of EXIF, with four gross anatomy arrows. Spikelet attachment positions and sheath-region hairs are shown, NOT bristle origin, separate glume nerves, mm dimensions or the authentic true ligule.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole flowering head next to centimeter ruler, showing interrupted spacing
Several intact mature spikelet bases viewed 10–20×: bristles absent on some branches or 2–8 mm when present
Short knotty rhizome and attached culm on legal collection
Actual 1–2 mm stiff-hair ligule distinct from longer nearby collar hairs
Spikelet/glume macro with mm scale; native county audit remains unchanged

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · INTERRUPTED NARROW PERENNIAL HEAD
field_id_short_tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: narrow upright flowering axis with visibly separated spikelet groups
field_id_short_tiles.details: Reverchon's bristlegrass is a perennial with short, sometimes knotty rhizomes; culms roughly 30–90 cm. Panicles ~5–20 cm may look interrupted, unlike the longer loose bottlebrush of S. scheelei. Archived image indices 0–2 support gross head shape but cannot verify a rooted rhizome or bristle insertion.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD PHOTO — SAME-PLANT RHIZOME AND HEAD NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TRUE STIFF-HAIR LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: At the blade–sheath junction find a ~1–2 mm fringe of stiff hairs
field_id_short_tiles.details: Do not mistake longer collar or sheath hairs for the ligule. Blade width roughly 1–7 mm, varying with position. No current image clearly isolates the actual 1–2 mm hair fringe with a scale; a source-labelled leaf without a visible junction is not ligule proof.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · SPARSE PERSISTENT BRISTLES
field_id_short_tiles.short: At each attached spikelet base, bristles may be absent or sparse, ~2–8 mm where present (FNA)
field_id_short_tiles.details: The regional UT treatment reports shorter curved bristles to ~2 mm; FNA documents ~2–8 mm. Do not impose a universal ≤2 mm rule. These are persistent sterile branchlets, NOT lemma awns. Existing panicle overview does not resolve insertion or allow counting. Sample multiple ripe attachments under 10–20×.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MATURE SPIKELET ~2.1–4.5 MM
field_id_short_tiles.short: Measure several ripe elliptical spikelets with a 1-mm bar; UT local ~3–3.6 mm
field_id_short_tiles.details: The lower glume is about HALF spikelet length, usually 5–7-veined; upper glume nearly reaches the fertile lemma, usually 7–9-veined. These proportional characters are from botanical treatments, not existing photos. Avoid inventing exact millimeters for separate glumes without a specimen.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — SEPARATED GLUMES AND CALIBRATED SPIKELET

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · WRINKLED FERTILE LEMMA, NO LONG AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma near fertile lemma length; hard upper fertile lemma finely cross-wrinkled
field_id_short_tiles.details: The upper fertile lemma and palea are firm; the lower sterile palea is absent in the cited FNA description. No projecting long true glume/lemma awn; visible bristles belong to sterile branchlets. Photograph a mature dissected ~2.1–4.5 mm spikelet and true transverse rugosity before annotating.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · COMPARE THREE LOCAL FOXTAILS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Sparse interrupted head versus S. parviflora's many bristles and S. scheelei's long mostly solitary bristles
field_id_short_tiles.details: S. parviflora commonly has 4–12 bristles per spikelet and a shorter denser head; S. scheelei usually one conspicuous 10–35 mm bristle with a tapering head; S. italica is a fibrous-rooted annual with heavy dense head. Counts and head silhouettes overlap in poor photos: check mature spikelet base, true ligule and rooted perennial habit.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED BRISTLE BASES PENDING

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: Authenticated rooted short-knotty-rhizome perennial with full 5–20 cm interrupted panicle in same frame, cm scale.
Several ripe spikelet bases at 10–20×, documenting truly absent/present persistent bristles and actual 2–8 mm lengths with mm bar.
Exposed true 1–2 mm stiff-hair ligule at blade/sheath junction separate from collar hairs.
Dissected 2.1–4.5 mm mature spikelet with lower/upper glumes, sterile lemma and finely cross-wrinkled fertile lemma, 1-mm scale; matched S. parviflora/S. scheelei attachments.
